Hi Markus / Kimberly,

Thanks for taking this on. We need to validate how telemetry (logs + traces + metrics) can be exported from our on-prem enclave to our Splunk Cloud instance without exposing sensitive payloads. Our requirements:

- Use an eBPF sidecar on the host to capture application traces and network metadata (low-overhead).
- Forward aggregated events to an internal Kafka cluster in the DMZ, then to a Splunk HEC ingest gateway in our VPC.
- Ensure a deterministic audit trail for custody and retention (30/90/365 day buckets).
- No direct outbound connections from enclave compute to internet.

We attached an initial sketch (ebpf-proxy-arch-v1.pdf) and a runbook stub (transfer-runbook.md). Key questions: can Redwood Private run a sidecar like this? How do you recommend signing/rotating tokens for HEC, and what telemetry sampling guarantees can you offer without losing trace continuity?

Hi Sasha — thanks for the detail and the artifacts. High-level responses below; I'll pull Kimberly and Marissa into specific action items.

1) eBPF sidecar model: Redwood Private can support a lightweight host-side collector (we run a vetted eBPF capture binary in the node agent). We typically stream only metadata and sanitized spans (no full request bodies) to the local aggregator. Well need your policy on PII scrubbing at the source to finalize.

2) Kafka DMZ pattern: supported. Our preferred flow is: host agent -> local aggregator (in-cluster) -> DMZ-forwarder (TLS to Kafka) -> bridge consumer in a hardened subnet. This lets you enforce outbound egress controls.

3) HEC auth: recommend short-lived mTLS client certs issued by your internal CA + per-connector API keys rotated by our runtime every 24 hours. We can also proxy HEC through a dedicated forwarder in a bastion VPC to centralize auditing.

4) Sampling / trace continuity: we use deterministic sampling keys (trace_id-based hashing) so you get consistent sampling across services; we can guarantee span linkage for up to 1 week of retention in the fast KV cache and longer in the cold store (depending on retention tier).

Next steps (proposed):
- Kimberly: confirm network port mapping and firewall rule template.
- Marissa: provide Splunk ingest pattern and required HEC header expectations; coordinate a proof of concept for checksum-based evidence handoff.
- Markus (me): run a short mock in our lab and share a hardened runbook for your SOC review.

I'll schedule a 30-min sync for tomorrow at 11:00 PT unless you prefer a different time.

Regards,
Markus Klein
Head of Product, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Sasha — quick note on ports and firewall constraints so you can review before the call: 

- Host eBPF agent -> local aggregator: TCP 4317 (OTLP) or UDP 514 for legacy syslog (internal only).
- Aggregator -> DMZ Kafka: TLS on 9093 (mutual TLS).
- DMZ forwarder -> Splunk HEC (bastion): TLS 443 to HEC endpoint; we recommend using private IP forwarding through a dedicated NAT/VPC endpoint so there is no direct internet egress.
- Health checks and orchestration: 8080 (internal), SSH 2222 (management jump host, restricted).

Network notes: please ensure kernel module policies allow eBPF programs from our vendor binary; otherwise we'll fall back to a userspace shim. Also confirm whether your Kafka cluster requires client certificates signed by a sub-CA (we support either).

I'll attach a firewall template in the drive link (see related_links). I'll also bring the Splunk ingest schema to the call.

Following up after the lab run and the call: quick summary and acceptance criteria for the POC.

POC scope (48 hours):
- Deploy eBPF capture as a node daemonset in your staging enclave (read-only capture of headers/metadata).
- Run the Redwood aggregator in a protected subnet; forward sanitized events to your Kafka DMZ using mTLS.
- Bridge consumer will deliver to a Splunk HEC endpoint behind the bastion; verify event checksum and insertion timestamp.
- Produce an evidence bundle: sample payloads (sanitized), HMACs, and transfer logs for SOC review.

Acceptance criteria:
- No sensitive payload fields appear in the Splunk events (SOC verification).
- End-to-end trace continuity for at least 80% of sampled requests under 95th-percentile load.
- Rotated certs/APIs are used and logged — rotation demonstrated by automated job.
- Audit trail: every transfer shows a signed handoff entry in the runbook (transfer-runbook.md).

I ran a quick lab test and attached the trimmed runbook and the lab findings to the Drive link (see related_links). For the cert rotation flow, we can optionally plug into your Vault/HSM to avoid storing keys on the forwarder.

If SOC signs off on the sanitized samples, we'll package the runbook and propose a 90-day retention tier for aggregated traces and 365-day cold retention for checksums and transfer logs.

Markus/Kimberly: please confirm any outstanding blockers — otherwise I'll create the Jira (OPS-1423) and request access for your staging environment.

Best,
Marissa Cole
